blocks.text: If you experience latency issues during your isolation session, you can check the latency information for the isolated browser in the Network Latency window.
To view the Network Latency window for your active isolated session:

blocks.item: Click the checkmark Zero Trust Mode icon. To learn more, see Using the Zero Trust Mode Menu in Native Browser Experience.

The Network Latency window appears. This window has live, real-time statistics of network latency for WebSocket and HTTP connectivity. The percentile statistics indicate the distribution of latency across pings. You can view the logs of each type of connectivity and review the following statistics:
Last value: The latency of the last ping
Number of pings: The total number of pings sent
99%: 99% of pings have latency that is less than or equal to the indicated value (e.g., 133 ms).
75%: 75% of pings have latency that is less than or equal to the indicated value (e.g., 96 ms).
50Mean: 50% of pings have latency that is less than or equal to the indicated value (e.g., 94 ms).
Std. deviation: The variance in latency across pings

blocks.text: If you notice latency statistics that are unusually high or inconsistent, you can save the information captured in the Network Latency window to share as a report with Zscaler Support to further diagnose the issue.
To save the Network Latency information as a report:

blocks.item: Click Export Logs. By default, the report is saved to your device as a text file.

blocks.text: You can email Zscaler Support with the Network Latency report attached and note the latency issues you've experienced.
